bib.title: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models

question: How can the context window of RoPE-based LLMs be extended efficiently, with and without fine-tuning?
hypothesis: Per-dimension (wavelength-aware) interpolation plus an attention temperature beats uniform position interpolation and NTK-aware scaling at lower training cost.
contributions: A complete account of the previously unpublished NTK-aware, Dynamic NTK and NTK-by-parts interpolations
YaRN: NTK-by-parts interpolation plus attention scaling by temperature t
Llama 2 7B and 13B extended to 64k and 128k with 400 (+200) steps
Dynamic Scaling for extension without fine-tuning

method.summary: Fine-tunes Llama 2 7B/13B with modified RoPE frequencies (NTK-by-parts, alpha=1, beta=32) and attention logit scaling sqrt(1/t)=0.1 ln(s)+1, at s=16 for 400 steps on 64k PG19 chunks then s=32 for 200 more. Evaluates sliding-window perplexity, passkey retrieval and the Open LLM suite against PI, NTK-aware, NTK-by-parts, Together and Code Llama.
method.task: context window extension of RoPE language models

datasets.name: PG19
datasets.size: chunked into 64k-token segments (128k models) or 32k segments (ablation); total size not stated
datasets.preprocessing: chunked, each segment bookended with BOS and EOS

datasets.name: Proof-pile
datasets.size: 10 random test documents with at least 128k tokens
datasets.preprocessing: truncated to context sizes 2k to 128k in 2k steps

datasets.name: RedPajama sample
datasets.preprocessing: used to study attention temperature (App A.3); also used by LLongMA-2 baseline

training.steps: 400 at s=16; s=32 starts from the s=16 checkpoint and adds 200; ablation 400 steps at s=16
training.hardware: A100 (PyTorch FSDP, Flash Attention 2); GPU count not stated

other.tokens_inferred: inferred: 400 steps x 64 x 64k = about 1.6B tokens for s=16; the paper states no token count

inference.samples: passkey: 50 iterations (32k LLaMA 7B), 10 iterations (64k/128k models); perplexity on 10 documents; no seeds
inference.prompting: Open LLM suite: ARC-c 25-shot, HellaSwag 10-shot, MMLU 5-shot, TruthfulQA 0-shot; passkey prompt format not given

metrics.name: sliding-window perplexity
metrics.definition: Press et al. 2022 sliding window, S=256

metrics.name: passkey accuracy
metrics.definition: retrieve a five-digit passkey from filler text; averaged over context sizes up to the largest with accuracy >= 80%

eval.protocol: Single runs, no seeds or significance tests; perplexity on 10 Proof-pile docs and 50 GovReport docs.

evidence.quote: We used a learning rate of 2 × 10−5 with no weight decay and a linear warmup of 20 steps

limits: Single runs, no seeds, confidence intervals or tests; perplexity from ten Proof-pile documents.
Perplexity is not a reliable indicator of effective context: authors hypothesise it 'may not be a great indicator'; passkey is a simple retrieval task, not reasoning.
Passkey accuracy averages over sizes up to the passkey context only, so the reported 99.4% excludes sizes where accuracy was below 80%.
No pre-training token count or total fine-tuning token count given; the 0.1% figure is unverifiable from the text.
Temperature formula fit on LLaMA/Llama 2 only; authors say alpha, beta must be tuned per model family.
Benchmark drops are larger for 13B (MMLU 55.8 to 51.9); the PG19 domain shift is blamed.
Dynamic scaling evidence is a single GovReport sample (Fig 8).
Code Llama comparisons are confounded by its code-specialised extra training.
ReRoPE and LM-Infinite not compared because they modify attention.

terms.definition: interpolate by s dims with r(d) < alpha, leave dims with r(d) > beta, ramp between
update s = max(1, l'/L) at each forward pass
